transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess... what brought me in is I keep hearing this man’s voice. It comes right out of the garage vents at the shop, and sometimes from under the hood when I'm working. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, just talking away. He keeps telling me not to trust my husband, and he warns me not to touch certain cars. 

Which is a real problem because I'm a mechanic, so I kind of have to work on them. Like this one Chevy we had in on Tuesday, the transmission was completely shot. The guy driving it tried to say it just started slipping, but the fluid was burnt black. People never maintain their cars. I actually took a couple years of college before I started turning wrenches, thought I wanted to do business management. But sitting in those lecture halls... the fluorescent lights always gave me a headache. My sister works in an office with those lights, I don't know how she does it. She just got a new dog, actually. A golden retriever mix. 

But yeah, anyway... the voice in the vents just keeps telling me my husband is up to something.
Have you used any drugs or stimulants, like meth, cocaine, or cannabis, around the time these voices started?

Drugs? No. No, I don't mess with any of that stuff. I mean, I drink coffee in the mornings, but that's it. The guys at the shop, though, they drink a ton of those Monster energy drinks. The big green ones with the claw marks on the can? They leave the empties everywhere, it drives me absolutely crazy. You can't just leave trash around a customer's car. 

One time, my coworker Dave left a half-empty can sitting on the cowl of a Ford F-150 and it knocked over and spilled right down into the AC intake. The whole cabin smelled like fake sugar and chemicals for a week. The customer was so mad, he threatened to leave a one-star Yelp review. Which, honestly, Yelp is basically useless now anyway, don't you think? It's all just people complaining because they want free stuff or they're having a bad day. I actually tried to leave a good review for this diner I went to with my husband a few weeks ago—they make these really incredible blueberry pancakes with the crispy edges, cooked in real butter—but I couldn't remember my password to log in to the app. I think it was my old dog's name, Buster, with some numbers after it, but I couldn't figure it out so I just gave up. I miss Buster. He was a good dog.
Have you ever had a head injury or a medical condition affecting your brain before these voices started?

A head injury? No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I bump my head on the undercarriage of cars sometimes when I'm rolling around on the creeper, but never hard enough to go to the hospital or anything. You really have to be careful under there, though, especially with the older rust buckets. The rust just flakes right off into your eyes if you aren't wearing your safety glasses. 

I always wear mine. My boss, Rick, he buys the absolute cheapest safety glasses in bulk, the ones that scratch if you just look at them wrong. He’s always cutting corners to save a buck. Like last month, he switched our shop towels to this terrible brand that leaves red lint everywhere. You wipe down a dipstick and it looks like it's growing fuzz. My husband actually hates finding those red towels mixed in with my work clothes. He does the laundry most of the time, which is nice, but he uses this lavender detergent that smells way too strong. It reminds me of my grandmother's house. She used to have these little bowls of dried purple flowers sitting around in every single room... potpourri, I think it's called? It always made me sneeze. She had this huge collection of ceramic cats, too. Hundreds of them just staring at you from the shelves.
Have you had a time when you felt unusually energized or high for several days?

Yeah, actually, I do get like that sometimes. I'll get this feeling like I'm just... flying high, you know? Like I have so much energy I could fix every single car in the whole town, no problem. I'll stay up late, I'll be working on projects, just feeling unstoppable. But then... if my husband asks me something stupid, like why the dishes aren't done, or if one of the other techs at the shop moves my socket set—even just an inch—I completely blow up. I get so mad, like they're doing it on purpose just to hold me down or mess with my head. 

Which is exactly why I hate sharing tools. You buy a good set of Snap-on wrenches, and it costs an arm and a leg, but they have that lifetime warranty. The guy on the tool truck, Gary, he comes by every Thursday. He's always trying to sell me these new diagnostic scanners, but I tell him, Gary, I don't need a fancy tablet to tell me what's wrong with an engine, I can hear it. My dad was the same way. He could listen to a tractor run for five seconds and tell you exactly which valve was ticking. He grew up on a farm, actually, out in Nebraska. Corn as far as you could see. I visited once when I was a kid, and I got lost in the cornfield for like three hours. It was terrifying. The stalks are so tall, and they all look exactly the same, and the wind makes this rustling sound that almost sounds like whispering... kind of like that voice in the vents, actually. Just... whispering all the time.
Have you ever had a brain illness, like seizures, a stroke, or an infection, around the time the voice started?

Brain illness? No, no, I haven't had any seizures or strokes or anything like that. I've always been pretty healthy, honestly. I mean, I try to take care of myself. I take those gummy vitamins every morning. The ones that taste like orange? Though lately they've been making them a little too sweet, I think. They probably changed the recipe to save money, just like how they changed the recipe for my favorite brand of peanut butter. 

It used to be so creamy, and now it just separates in the jar and you have to stir it forever. And if you don't stir it right, you get all this oil at the top and dry crumbles at the bottom. It ruins a good piece of toast. I usually have toast before work, with a little bit of butter. Real butter, not that margarine stuff. My husband bought margarine once by mistake, and I couldn't even look at it. It's basically plastic, isn't it? Just chemicals whipped up to look like food. That's what they do with everything now. Everything is just fake and cheap. Like those plastic clips that hold the bumper covers on the newer cars. You try to pop one out with a flathead, and it just shatters into a million pieces. Then you have to dig around in the parts bin for a replacement, and you never have the right size. It's so frustrating.
Did the voice start while you were using any drugs or stimulants, or only after you had stopped them?

Drugs? No, definitely not. I don't touch any of that garbage. I mean, stimulants... unless you count caffeine? I practically live on those white Monster energy drinks when the shop gets backed up. Though I actually had to stop leaving them in the breakroom fridge because someone kept taking them. I'm like ninety percent sure it's Kyle from the lube bay. He's always hanging around the fridge looking suspicious right before the lunch truck pulls up. 

The guy who drives the lunch truck, Hector, he makes these incredible al pastor tacos, but he absolutely buries them in cilantro. I don't mind it, but my sister, she has that genetic thing where cilantro tastes exactly like dish soap. We went out for her birthday last year to this fancy place downtown, and she sent her food back three times because they kept putting it on her plate as a garnish. The waiter was getting so annoyed, sighing and rolling his eyes and everything. Customer service is just completely dead these days, you know? It's like nobody takes pride in their work anymore. You see it with the new techs all the time. They'll strip the threads on an oil pan drain plug and just try to hide it with RTV silicone instead of fixing it right. And then guess who has to drill it out when the customer comes back a week later complaining about a puddle on their driveway? Me. It's always me having to clean up everybody else's messes.
Have you ever had a period of several days when your mood was very high or irritable at the same time as the voice got worse?

Yeah, actually, that's exactly how it happens. Like those times I was telling you about, when I'm barely sleeping and just racing around the shop with all these big plans? That's when it all happens at once. I'll be hearing that voice from the vents the whole time, and I get absolutely certain that the battery chargers and the shop cameras are being used to watch me. 

Which is wild because our shop cameras are mostly ancient anyway. Well, the ones in the front office are old. The boss actually just put in these brand new 4K dome cameras out in the bays. He claims it's for insurance purposes, but I know it's because he thinks the night shift is stealing oil filters. Which they probably are, honestly. The night shift guys are a complete joke. They leave the air hoses uncoiled all over the floor, which is a massive tripping hazard. OSHA would have a field day if they walked in at six in the morning. I tripped over a pneumatic line last Tuesday and almost dropped a transmission pan full of fluid. 

Have you ever smelled burnt transmission fluid? It is the worst smell in the entire world. It gets in your clothes, your hair, your skin... I had to wash my uniform three times with heavy-duty citrus degreaser just to get the stink out. My washing machine at home still smells a little weird from it. It's an old top-loader, one of those original Maytags with the mechanical timer. You really can't kill those things. The new ones with the digital computer boards, one little power surge and the whole machine is just a brick. It's exactly like the newer cars. Everything is run by modules now, so you can't just turn a wrench, you have to reprogram the whole system just to change a battery. It drives me crazy. But anyway, yeah, when I'm all wound up and not sleeping, that's when the vent voice is just constantly going, and I know those chargers are watching me.
Have you ever heard the voice or believed the cameras were watching you when your mood was not high or irritable?

Yeah, actually, I do. Even when I'm not all wound up, you know? Like, there was this stretch a little while back, a few weeks where things were just... quiet. I was sleeping normally, getting my solid eight hours, and I wasn't rushing around making all those big plans. But the voice from the vents was still there. And I still knew, I just knew, that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

My husband actually bought this new smartwatch around that time. One of those ones that tracks your sleep and your heart rate and everything. He's obsessed with it. He checks it constantly to see how many steps he's taken, like it's a game or something. I don't get the appeal of those things, honestly. Having something strapped to your wrist that just constantly buzzes with notifications? It would drive me insane. I already have enough going on with my phone. The shop group chat alone is a nightmare. The service writer, Dave, he texts us all these "motivational" quotes at like six in the morning. It's so annoying. And he uses way too many emojis. Who uses the fire emoji when they're talking about an oil change special? Dave, that's who. He used to be a salesman at a dealership before he came to our shop, and you can totally tell. He still has that slick, pushy energy, always trying to upsell people on things they don't need, like engine flushes on cars with twenty thousand miles. I hate doing those flushes anyway. The chemicals smell terrible, and half the time it just loosens up gunk that ends up clogging the oil pickup screen later. Then the customer comes back furious because their engine is knocking, and Dave just shrugs it off and blames the technicians. But yeah, even when I was feeling totally level and sleeping fine, that voice was still going, and I knew they were keeping tabs on me.
About how long have you been hearing the voice or believing people are watching you?

It's been going on for a while now, probably about ten months since the voices and the tracking stuff really started. Ten months... wow, that means it started right around the time the shop got that new Snap-on tool truck guy. The old guy, Gary, he retired and moved down to Florida. Bought a place right on the water, actually. He used to bring us donuts every Tuesday, the good kind from that bakery over on 4th Street. The new guy, though, he doesn't bring anything. And his prices are absolutely outrageous. I mean, I know Snap-on is expensive, but he was trying to charge me a hundred and fifty bucks for a single 10-millimeter socket. Just one! And you know how it is with 10-millimeters, they literally just vanish into thin air. I swear there's a black hole somewhere in the shop that just swallows them up. I must have bought at least twenty of them over the last few years. My husband tells me I need to be more organized, but he doesn't get it. He works in an office, sitting at a desk all day looking at spreadsheets. He doesn't understand what it's like when you're elbow-deep in an engine bay and you drop a socket down behind the alternator and you just hear it go 'clink, clink, clink' all the way down to the skid plate. You can spend an hour just trying to fish it out with a magnet. So yeah, I just buy extras. But anyway, yeah, it's been about ten months of all this happening.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least a month when the voice or the belief that you were being watched continued even though your mood was completely normal?

Yeah, definitely. I think I was just saying this a minute ago, but yeah, there was a stretch that lasted for, oh, probably a month, maybe six weeks? Where things were just... quiet. Like my mood was totally normal, I wasn't making all those huge plans, and I was actually sleeping more. But even during that whole time, I still heard the garage voice, and I still absolutely believed my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

I was getting a ton of sleep then, though. We actually bought a new mattress right around that time. It was one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a tight little box. It is wild how they compress a whole king-size bed into something the size of a mini-fridge. The delivery guy just dumped it on our front porch and it weighed like a hundred and fifty pounds. I had to drag it inside by myself because my husband was at work. And when you cut the plastic open, it just aggressively expands. It smells terrible for the first few days, too. Off-gassing, they call it. Smells like a chemical factory. 

Honestly, it smells exactly like the parts cleaner we use at the shop, that heavy-duty solvent we soak the old carburetors in. You have to wear these thick rubber gloves all the way up to your elbows when you use that stuff or it'll just eat your skin right off. Dave, that service writer I was telling you about, he actually accidentally leaned against the parts washer once and ruined a pair of his fancy slacks. It was hilarious, he was so mad. He tried to expense a new pair to the shop, but the boss just laughed at him. But anyway, yeah, it was definitely a month or more where I was totally level, but all the voice and tracking stuff was still going on.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or believing you were being watched, but you were not having any manic or very depressed symptoms at all?

I feel like we're kind of going in circles here, doc, but yeah, absolutely. Like I was just saying, even during that quieter few weeks when I was actually sleeping more and wasn't making all those huge plans, I still heard the garage voice, and I still fully believed my husband and my boss were tracking me. So it definitely lasted longer than two weeks. 

Two weeks is actually the exact amount of time we had this '69 Chevelle sitting on my lift recently. Just taking up my entire bay because we were waiting on a specialized steering column part. The supply chain stuff for classic cars is still a total joke right now. You order something, they tell you three days, and then it's two weeks of dead air. And the customer, this older guy named Richard, he kept calling the shop every single day at 1:00 PM. Like clockwork. Dave, of course, kept promising him it would be done "tomorrow," which just made Richard so much madder when tomorrow came and it wasn't done. Dave has zero spine when it comes to managing customer expectations. He just tells them what they want to hear to get them off the phone. Like, just tell the guy the part is stuck in a warehouse in Ohio! It's not that hard. I ended up having to get on the phone with Richard myself, wiping grease off my hands so I wouldn't ruin the receiver, just to explain the shipping delay to him. He was actually really nice once someone just told him the truth. He even brought us a Box O' Joe from Dunkin when he finally picked the car up. 

But anyway, yeah, I definitely had a few weeks of being totally normal mood-wise while all the tracking and voice stuff was still happening.
When your mood is not high or irritable, do the voice and the belief that people are watching you still happen?

I mean, doc, are you even listening to me? I feel like I've said this three times now. Yes. Even when my mood is totally fine, not high, not irritable. Like that quieter stretch of a few weeks I keep bringing up, where I was sleeping a lot more and I wasn't running around making those huge plans... the voice in the garage was still there, and I still knew for a fact that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It's like talking to Dave the service writer, honestly. You tell him a car needs new rotors, you write it on the ticket, you tell him to his face, and then an hour later he comes back and asks if the rotors are good. Like, no, Dave! I literally just told you! He does this thing where he clicks his pen constantly when you're talking to him, too. Just click-click-click-click-click. It drives me absolutely up the wall. Especially when I'm trying to listen to an engine idle to diagnose a misfire, and he's standing right there clicking that stupid blue pen. I swear one of these days I'm going to take that pen and drop it right into a pan of used motor oil. The thick, sludgy stuff that comes out of diesels. Good luck clicking it then, Dave. But yeah, to answer your question again, yes, the voice and the tracking stuff still happen even when my mood is completely normal.
Do you believe the voice or the people watching you are sending messages or controlling your thoughts in some special way?

No, I don't think they're sending me messages or controlling my thoughts or anything sci-fi like that. It's just... I know it sounds far-fetched, but I'm still convinced my husband and the shop owner have been using the EV chargers and the security cameras to track what I'm doing. Even when they show me the footage and say there's nothing there, I just know they're watching me. 

Those EV chargers, by the way, are a total nightmare to install. We just put two of them in at the shop because the boss thinks we're going to start getting all this Tesla business. Like, sure, buddy. The people driving hundred-thousand-dollar electric cars are definitely bringing them to a greasy independent shop next to a strip mall. But anyway, the wiring for those things is intense. You have to run this heavy-gauge conduit all the way from the main breaker panel, and of course, our panel is all the way in the back corner behind the tire rack. We had to move like fifty tires just to get to it. And they're not the light ones either, they're those massive all-terrain truck tires. My back was killing me for a week after that. I told Dave he should help, but he just gave me this look and said he had to "manage the front desk." Yeah, right. Managing his fantasy football team, more like it. But yeah, no mind control or anything, just the tracking with the cameras and the chargers.
Have the voice and the belief that people are watching you ever continued for at least two weeks while you were also having no manic or depressed episode?

Doc, I really feel like you're messing with me now. I know I've answered this exact question like four times. But yes. Yes, they did. Like I said before, even during that quieter few weeks when I was sleeping more and wasn't making those huge plans, I still heard the garage voice and I still knew my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It's literally exactly like dealing with the parts department at the dealership down the road. You call them up, you give them the VIN, you tell them exactly what part you need—like, say, a mass airflow sensor for a 2015 F-150. You spell it out for them. And then the guy on the phone, usually it's this kid named Tyler who sounds like he's half asleep, he goes, "Okay, so you need a MAP sensor?" No, Tyler! Mass airflow! MAF! I just said it! It's like the words go into their ears and just vanish into a black hole. And then when the delivery guy finally shows up, half the time it's the wrong part anyway. Last week they sent me a water pump for a completely different engine block. I had the customer's truck all torn apart on the lift, coolant drained, and I open the box and it's not even close to fitting. I had to leave the truck tying up my bay overnight while Tyler figured out how to read a parts diagram. But yeah, to answer your question again, yes, the voice and the tracking kept going for at least two weeks even when my mood was totally normal.
Have these experiences made it harder for you to work or keep up with daily life?

Yeah, it definitely has. I mean, I’ve been making mistakes at the shop lately, which isn't like me at all. They actually pulled me off all the high-voltage EV work because they said they were worried I wasn’t being safe with it. 

Which, by the way, high voltage is no joke. You’re dealing with like 400 to 800 volts in some of these newer battery packs. You have to wear these thick Class 0 rubber gloves with leather protectors over them, and let me tell you, they get so incredibly sweaty in the summer. You’re trying to carefully disconnect a high-voltage interlock loop and your hands are just swimming in sweat inside the rubber. And if you drop a wrench across the wrong terminals... boom. Arc flash. It’s literally like a lightning bolt right in your face. I saw a guy at my old shop melt a 10-millimeter socket right to a battery post once. The whole bay smelled like ozone and burnt hair for a week. He didn’t even get fired for that, which is crazy when you think about it, but they pull *me* off just because I'm distracted by the cameras? Whatever. 

But yeah, it’s not just work. At home, the fighting with my husband about the tracking and everything just got worse and worse. It got so bad that he finally just packed me into the car and took me in for an emergency evaluation. 

He made me ride in his Prius to get there, too, which I absolutely hate riding in. The suspension is so mushy, it feels like you’re driving a marshmallow. I keep telling him I can put some stiffer struts on it, maybe upgrade the rear sway bar so it actually handles like a real vehicle, but he won’t let me touch it. He always says, "It’s a commuter car, not a race car." Like, I’m not trying to make it a race car, Mark, I’m just trying to make it so I don’t get seasick going around a basic cloverleaf on-ramp! It drives me crazy. But anyway... what was the question? Oh, yeah, daily life. Yeah, it's been a lot harder to keep up with things.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when you felt so energized or irritable that you needed very little sleep?

Yeah, absolutely. There have been times, like for weeks at a stretch, where I'd sleep maybe two or three hours a night. I'd wake up way before dawn, and my mind would already be at the garage, thinking about all the work I could get done. It just felt like sleeping any more than that was a total waste of time when I had so much energy. 

Speaking of waking up early, the sunrise hitting the shop windows is actually really brutal if you're trying to read a scan tool. The glare is ridiculous. We have these big roll-up bay doors with those little rectangular windows in them, and the sun hits them at the exact wrong angle right around 6:30 in the morning. I told the boss we need to tint them or get some shades, but he just ignores me. He says it "lets the natural light in." Natural light, right. Tell that to my retinas when I'm trying to read live data off an OBD2 scanner on a car with a misfire. Have you ever tried to read fuel trim numbers on a tiny LCD screen while the sun is basically blasting a laser beam directly into your eyeball? It's impossible. You end up having to throw a jacket over your head and the scanner just to see the screen, and then you look like an idiot hiding under a coat in the driver's seat. And the scanners aren't cheap, either. The Snap-On one we have is like, five grand, and the screen is still awful in direct sunlight. But anyway, yeah, I'd only sleep a couple of hours and feel totally fine, just ready to go.
Have you ever heard the voice or believed you were being watched when you were not having any manic symptoms?

Doc, I feel like we're going in circles here. I know I just answered this. Yes, yes I did. Like I was saying before, even when I had that quieter stretch for a few weeks, where I was sleeping a normal amount and I wasn't running around making all those huge plans... I still heard the voice from the garage. And I still knew for a fact that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It's just like dealing with service writers, honestly. You tell them the exact diagnosis, you write it on the ticket—like, "customer states rattling noise over bumps, found worn sway bar links, needs replacement." You literally type it into the system. And then the service writer, who has never turned a wrench in his life, goes out to the waiting room and tells the customer they need new struts. No! I didn't say struts! Struts are like eight hundred bucks, sway bar links are fifty! And then the customer comes storming back into the bay yelling at me because they think I'm trying to rip them off. It's infuriating. The service writers just don't listen, they just hear "suspension" and try to upsell the most expensive thing. I swear, half my job is just fixing the communication breakdowns between the front desk and the customer. But yeah, to answer you again... yes, the voice and the tracking were still there even when I wasn't manic.
Have there been any times when the voice or the belief that you were being watched happened for at least two weeks while you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

Are you reading off a checklist or something? Because I really feel like we just went over this. But yes, to be specific, yes. There was a stretch of a few weeks where my mood was totally normal. I wasn't feeling down at all, I was sleeping a normal amount, and I wasn’t making any of those huge plans. But even during those quieter weeks, I still heard the garage voice, and I still knew for a fact my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

Which, honestly, is so ridiculously easy to do now. People think you have to be some kind of spy to track a car, or hardwire something into the fuse box, but you can literally buy a magnetic GPS unit online for thirty bucks and slap it on the inside of a frame rail in two seconds. Or those insurance dongles! Have you seen those? The insurance companies tell you to plug them into your OBD2 port under the dash to get a "safe driver discount," but it’s literally just a tracker. It logs your speed, your hard braking, your exact location... everything. 

We had a lady bring her car into the shop last month because her battery kept dying overnight. I hooked up my multimeter, doing a voltage drop test across all the fuses, and guess what? It was her stupid insurance tracker causing a parasitic draw. It was pulling like 300 milliamps while the car was off just so it could stay awake and beam her data back to corporate. I told her to yank it out and throw it in the trash. You can't trust anything you plug into a data port, they're basically just little snitches. 

But anyway... what did you ask? Oh, right, the two weeks. Yeah, for at least a couple weeks, I wasn't up or down, but the voice and the tracking stuff definitely didn't stop.
Have you ever had hallucinations or beliefs that people were watching you for at least two weeks when you were not having any mood episode at all?

Are you serious right now? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills. We literally just talked about this! I just said yes to this exact same question! 

But fine, yes, I'll say it again. Yes, there was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't manic, I wasn't depressed, I was sleeping fine, not making any wild plans... but I still heard the voice from the garage, and I still knew my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It’s like when a customer brings in a car for a check engine light, right? And you scan it, and it throws a P0420 code, which is catalyst system efficiency below threshold. So you tell the customer, "Hey, your catalytic converter is shot, it needs to be replaced." And they say, "Okay, but can you just clear the code and see if it comes back?" And you're like, "Buddy, I can clear the code, but the cat is still hollowed out, the code is going to come back the second the monitor runs." But they insist. So you clear it. They drive away. Two days later, they're back, complaining that the light is on again, asking the exact same question. "Why is the light on?" Because your catalytic converter is dead! I already told you this! It's like nobody listens to the actual diagnosis the first time. You can clear the code all you want, but the underlying problem doesn't just magically disappear because you hit a button on a scanner. 

Anyway. Yes. The voice and the tracking were still there for a few weeks even when my mood was totally normal. Can we please move on to a different question now?
Besides hearing the voice and feeling watched, do you ever have trouble keeping your thoughts or speech organized, like others say you’re hard to follow?

No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever told me I'm hard to follow. Sometimes I just have a lot to say, you know? Like, there's a lot going on in my head, especially when I'm trying to explain something complicated. 

But people usually get what I'm saying. Unless they're just not listening, which, like I said, happens all the time at the shop. Speaking of the shop, I actually need to get back there soon. We've got this nightmare of a job coming in this afternoon—a 2015 Ford F-150, the one with the 3.5 EcoBoost. The customer says it's got a rattle on cold start, which everyone knows is the cam phasers. It's always the cam phasers on those engines. Ford even put out a TSB on it, but the customer didn't want to pay for the repair when it was under warranty, and now they're out of the powertrain coverage and they're mad at us about the price. It's a huge job, you have to take the whole front cover off the engine, pull the valve covers... it's easily a twelve-hour job if you do it right. And the parts alone are a fortune because you have to replace the timing chain, the tensioners, the guides, everything while you're in there, otherwise they'll just be back in six months with a stretched chain. But try explaining that to a guy who just wants a cheap fix. He was in the waiting room yesterday just pacing around, looking at his phone... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my speech. No, I speak perfectly fine. My thoughts are organized. People just need to pay attention when I'm talking.

doctor.intent: Open the interview and identify the main presenting complaint.

patient.answer:
Well, I guess... what brought me in is I keep hearing this man’s voice. It comes right out of the garage vents at the shop, and sometimes from under the hood when I'm working. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, just talking away. He keeps telling me not to trust my husband, and he warns me not to touch certain cars. 

Which is a real problem because I'm a mechanic, so I kind of have to work on them. Like this one Chevy we had in on Tuesday, the transmission was completely shot. The guy driving it tried to say it just started slipping, but the fluid was burnt black. People never maintain their cars. I actually took a couple years of college before I started turning wrenches, thought I wanted to do business management. But sitting in those lecture halls... the fluorescent lights always gave me a headache. My sister works in an office with those lights, I don't know how she does it. She just got a new dog, actually. A golden retriever mix. 

But yeah, anyway... the voice in the vents just keeps telling me my husband is up to something.

inference.note: New onset auditory hallucinations with persecutory content raises primary psychotic disorders and substance/medical-induced psychosis; schizoaffective, brief psychotic, delusional, and schizophrenia spectrum remain possible. No clear evidence yet to rule any of these out.

patient.answer:
Drugs? No. No, I don't mess with any of that stuff. I mean, I drink coffee in the mornings, but that's it. The guys at the shop, though, they drink a ton of those Monster energy drinks. The big green ones with the claw marks on the can? They leave the empties everywhere, it drives me absolutely crazy. You can't just leave trash around a customer's car. 

One time, my coworker Dave left a half-empty can sitting on the cowl of a Ford F-150 and it knocked over and spilled right down into the AC intake. The whole cabin smelled like fake sugar and chemicals for a week. The customer was so mad, he threatened to leave a one-star Yelp review. Which, honestly, Yelp is basically useless now anyway, don't you think? It's all just people complaining because they want free stuff or they're having a bad day. I actually tried to leave a good review for this diner I went to with my husband a few weeks ago—they make these really incredible blueberry pancakes with the crispy edges, cooked in real butter—but I couldn't remember my password to log in to the app. I think it was my old dog's name, Buster, with some numbers after it, but I couldn't figure it out so I just gave up. I miss Buster. He was a good dog.

patient.answer:
A head injury? No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I bump my head on the undercarriage of cars sometimes when I'm rolling around on the creeper, but never hard enough to go to the hospital or anything. You really have to be careful under there, though, especially with the older rust buckets. The rust just flakes right off into your eyes if you aren't wearing your safety glasses. 

I always wear mine. My boss, Rick, he buys the absolute cheapest safety glasses in bulk, the ones that scratch if you just look at them wrong. He’s always cutting corners to save a buck. Like last month, he switched our shop towels to this terrible brand that leaves red lint everywhere. You wipe down a dipstick and it looks like it's growing fuzz. My husband actually hates finding those red towels mixed in with my work clothes. He does the laundry most of the time, which is nice, but he uses this lavender detergent that smells way too strong. It reminds me of my grandmother's house. She used to have these little bowls of dried purple flowers sitting around in every single room... potpourri, I think it's called? It always made me sneeze. She had this huge collection of ceramic cats, too. Hundreds of them just staring at you from the shelves.

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I’ll be flying high like I can fix every car in town and then, if my husband asks why the dishes aren’t done or a tech moves my socket set, I blow up like they’re trying to hold me down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have experienced periods of feeling unusually energized or 'high,' which corresponds to elevated or irritable mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah, actually, I do get like that sometimes. I'll get this feeling like I'm just... flying high, you know? Like I have so much energy I could fix every single car in the whole town, no problem. I'll stay up late, I'll be working on projects, just feeling unstoppable. But then... if my husband asks me something stupid, like why the dishes aren't done, or if one of the other techs at the shop moves my socket set—even just an inch—I completely blow up. I get so mad, like they're doing it on purpose just to hold me down or mess with my head. 

Which is exactly why I hate sharing tools. You buy a good set of Snap-on wrenches, and it costs an arm and a leg, but they have that lifetime warranty. The guy on the tool truck, Gary, he comes by every Thursday. He's always trying to sell me these new diagnostic scanners, but I tell him, Gary, I don't need a fancy tablet to tell me what's wrong with an engine, I can hear it. My dad was the same way. He could listen to a tractor run for five seconds and tell you exactly which valve was ticking. He grew up on a farm, actually, out in Nebraska. Corn as far as you could see. I visited once when I was a kid, and I got lost in the cornfield for like three hours. It was terrifying. The stalks are so tall, and they all look exactly the same, and the wind makes this rustling sound that almost sounds like whispering... kind of like that voice in the vents, actually. Just... whispering all the time.

Brain illness? No, no, I haven't had any seizures or strokes or anything like that. I've always been pretty healthy, honestly. I mean, I try to take care of myself. I take those gummy vitamins every morning. The ones that taste like orange? Though lately they've been making them a little too sweet, I think. They probably changed the recipe to save money, just like how they changed the recipe for my favorite brand of peanut butter. 

It used to be so creamy, and now it just separates in the jar and you have to stir it forever. And if you don't stir it right, you get all this oil at the top and dry crumbles at the bottom. It ruins a good piece of toast. I usually have toast before work, with a little bit of butter. Real butter, not that margarine stuff. My husband bought margarine once by mistake, and I couldn't even look at it. It's basically plastic, isn't it? Just chemicals whipped up to look like food. That's what they do with everything now. Everything is just fake and cheap. Like those plastic clips that hold the bumper covers on the newer cars. You try to pop one out with a flathead, and it just shatters into a million pieces. Then you have to dig around in the parts bin for a replacement, and you never have the right size. It's so frustrating.

Drugs? No, definitely not. I don't touch any of that garbage. I mean, stimulants... unless you count caffeine? I practically live on those white Monster energy drinks when the shop gets backed up. Though I actually had to stop leaving them in the breakroom fridge because someone kept taking them. I'm like ninety percent sure it's Kyle from the lube bay. He's always hanging around the fridge looking suspicious right before the lunch truck pulls up. 

The guy who drives the lunch truck, Hector, he makes these incredible al pastor tacos, but he absolutely buries them in cilantro. I don't mind it, but my sister, she has that genetic thing where cilantro tastes exactly like dish soap. We went out for her birthday last year to this fancy place downtown, and she sent her food back three times because they kept putting it on her plate as a garnish. The waiter was getting so annoyed, sighing and rolling his eyes and everything. Customer service is just completely dead these days, you know? It's like nobody takes pride in their work anymore. You see it with the new techs all the time. They'll strip the threads on an oil pan drain plug and just try to hide it with RTV silicone instead of fixing it right. And then guess who has to drill it out when the customer comes back a week later complaining about a puddle on their driveway? Me. It's always me having to clean up everybody else's messes.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a mood episode concurrent with the psychotic symptoms, which would help distinguish schizoaffective or bipolar disorder from schizophrenia and other causes.

patient.answer:
Yeah, actually, that's exactly how it happens. Like those times I was telling you about, when I'm barely sleeping and just racing around the shop with all these big plans? That's when it all happens at once. I'll be hearing that voice from the vents the whole time, and I get absolutely certain that the battery chargers and the shop cameras are being used to watch me. 

Which is wild because our shop cameras are mostly ancient anyway. Well, the ones in the front office are old. The boss actually just put in these brand new 4K dome cameras out in the bays. He claims it's for insurance purposes, but I know it's because he thinks the night shift is stealing oil filters. Which they probably are, honestly. The night shift guys are a complete joke. They leave the air hoses uncoiled all over the floor, which is a massive tripping hazard. OSHA would have a field day if they walked in at six in the morning. I tripped over a pneumatic line last Tuesday and almost dropped a transmission pan full of fluid. 

Have you ever smelled burnt transmission fluid? It is the worst smell in the entire world. It gets in your clothes, your hair, your skin... I had to wash my uniform three times with heavy-duty citrus degreaser just to get the stink out. My washing machine at home still smells a little weird from it. It's an old top-loader, one of those original Maytags with the mechanical timer. You really can't kill those things. The new ones with the digital computer boards, one little power surge and the whole machine is just a brick. It's exactly like the newer cars. Everything is run by modules now, so you can't just turn a wrench, you have to reprogram the whole system just to change a battery. It drives me crazy. But anyway, yeah, when I'm all wound up and not sleeping, that's when the vent voice is just constantly going, and I know those chargers are watching me.

patient.answer:
Yeah, actually, I do. Even when I'm not all wound up, you know? Like, there was this stretch a little while back, a few weeks where things were just... quiet. I was sleeping normally, getting my solid eight hours, and I wasn't rushing around making all those big plans. But the voice from the vents was still there. And I still knew, I just knew, that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

My husband actually bought this new smartwatch around that time. One of those ones that tracks your sleep and your heart rate and everything. He's obsessed with it. He checks it constantly to see how many steps he's taken, like it's a game or something. I don't get the appeal of those things, honestly. Having something strapped to your wrist that just constantly buzzes with notifications? It would drive me insane. I already have enough going on with my phone. The shop group chat alone is a nightmare. The service writer, Dave, he texts us all these "motivational" quotes at like six in the morning. It's so annoying. And he uses way too many emojis. Who uses the fire emoji when they're talking about an oil change special? Dave, that's who. He used to be a salesman at a dealership before he came to our shop, and you can totally tell. He still has that slick, pushy energy, always trying to upsell people on things they don't need, like engine flushes on cars with twenty thousand miles. I hate doing those flushes anyway. The chemicals smell terrible, and half the time it just loosens up gunk that ends up clogging the oil pickup screen later. Then the customer comes back furious because their engine is knocking, and Dave just shrugs it off and blames the technicians. But yeah, even when I was feeling totally level and sleeping fine, that voice was still going, and I knew they were keeping tabs on me.

patient.answer: It's been going on for a while now, probably about ten months since the voices and the tracking stuff really started. Ten months... wow, that means it started right around the time the shop got that new Snap-on tool truck guy. The old guy, Gary, he retired and moved down to Florida. Bought a place right on the water, actually. He used to bring us donuts every Tuesday, the good kind from that bakery over on 4th Street. The new guy, though, he doesn't bring anything. And his prices are absolutely outrageous. I mean, I know Snap-on is expensive, but he was trying to charge me a hundred and fifty bucks for a single 10-millimeter socket. Just one! And you know how it is with 10-millimeters, they literally just vanish into thin air. I swear there's a black hole somewhere in the shop that just swallows them up. I must have bought at least twenty of them over the last few years. My husband tells me I need to be more organized, but he doesn't get it. He works in an office, sitting at a desk all day looking at spreadsheets. He doesn't understand what it's like when you're elbow-deep in an engine bay and you drop a socket down behind the alternator and you just hear it go 'clink, clink, clink' all the way down to the skid plate. Yeah, definitely. I think I was just saying this a minute ago, but yeah, there was a stretch that lasted for, oh, probably a month, maybe six weeks? Where things were just... quiet. Like my mood was totally normal, I wasn't making all those huge plans, and I was actually sleeping more. But even during that whole time, I still heard the garage voice, and I still absolutely believed my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

I was getting a ton of sleep then, though. We actually bought a new mattress right around that time. It was one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a tight little box. It is wild how they compress a whole king-size bed into something the size of a mini-fridge. The delivery guy just dumped it on our front porch and it weighed like a hundred and fifty pounds. I had to drag it inside by myself because my husband was at work. And when you cut the plastic open, it just aggressively expands. It smells terrible for the first few days, too. Off-gassing, they call it. Smells like a chemical factory. 

Honestly, it smells exactly like the parts cleaner we use at the shop, that heavy-duty solvent we soak the old carburetors in. You have to wear these thick rubber gloves all the way up to your elbows when you use that stuff or it'll just eat your skin right off. Dave, that service writer I was telling you about, he actually accidentally leaned against the parts washer once and ruined a pair of his fancy slacks. It was hilarious, he was so mad. He tried to expense a new pair to the shop, but the boss just laughed at him. But anyway, yeah, it was definitely a month or more where I was totally level, but all the voice and tracking stuff was still going on.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a distinct period of elevated mood with a full psychotic episode lasting at least 2 weeks in the absence of mood symptoms, which would favor schizoaffective disorder over bipolar I disorder with psychotic features or delusional disorder.

patient.answer:
I feel like we're kind of going in circles here, doc, but yeah, absolutely. Like I was just saying, even during that quieter few weeks when I was actually sleeping more and wasn't making all those huge plans, I still heard the garage voice, and I still fully believed my husband and my boss were tracking me. So it definitely lasted longer than two weeks. 

Two weeks is actually the exact amount of time we had this '69 Chevelle sitting on my lift recently. Just taking up my entire bay because we were waiting on a specialized steering column part. The supply chain stuff for classic cars is still a total joke right now. You order something, they tell you three days, and then it's two weeks of dead air. And the customer, this older guy named Richard, he kept calling the shop every single day at 1:00 PM. Like clockwork. Dave, of course, kept promising him it would be done "tomorrow," which just made Richard so much madder when tomorrow came and it wasn't done. Dave has zero spine when it comes to managing customer expectations. He just tells them what they want to hear to get them off the phone. Like, just tell the guy the part is stuck in a warehouse in Ohio! It's not that hard. I ended up having to get on the phone with Richard myself, wiping grease off my hands so I wouldn't ruin the receiver, just to explain the shipping delay to him. He was actually really nice once someone just told him the truth. He even brought us a Box O' Joe from Dunkin when he finally picked the car up. 

But anyway, yeah, I definitely had a few weeks of being totally normal mood-wise while all the tracking and voice stuff was still happening.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are confined to mood episodes or persist independently, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.

patient.answer:
I mean, doc, are you even listening to me? I feel like I've said this three times now. Yes. Even when my mood is totally fine, not high, not irritable. Like that quieter stretch of a few weeks I keep bringing up, where I was sleeping a lot more and I wasn't running around making those huge plans... the voice in the garage was still there, and I still knew for a fact that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It's like talking to Dave the service writer, honestly. You tell him a car needs new rotors, you write it on the ticket, you tell him to his face, and then an hour later he comes back and asks if the rotors are good. Like, no, Dave! I literally just told you! He does this thing where he clicks his pen constantly when you're talking to him, too. Just click-click-click-click-click. It drives me absolutely up the wall. Especially when I'm trying to listen to an engine idle to diagnose a misfire, and he's standing right there clicking that stupid blue pen. I swear one of these days I'm going to take that pen and drop it right into a pan of used motor oil. The thick, sludgy stuff that comes out of diesels. Good luck clicking it then, Dave. But yeah, to answer your question again, yes, the voice and the tracking stuff still happen even when my mood is completely normal.

No, I don't think they're sending me messages or controlling my thoughts or anything sci-fi like that. It's just... I know it sounds far-fetched, but I'm still convinced my husband and the shop owner have been using the EV chargers and the security cameras to track what I'm doing. Even when they show me the footage and say there's nothing there, I just know they're watching me. 

Those EV chargers, by the way, are a total nightmare to install. We just put two of them in at the shop because the boss thinks we're going to start getting all this Tesla business. patient.answer:
Doc, I really feel like you're messing with me now. I know I've answered this exact question like four times. But yes. Yes, they did. Like I said before, even during that quieter few weeks when I was sleeping more and wasn't making those huge plans, I still heard the garage voice and I still knew my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It's literally exactly like dealing with the parts department at the dealership down the road. You call them up, you give them the VIN, you tell them exactly what part you need—like, say, a mass airflow sensor for a 2015 F-150. You spell it out for them. And then the guy on the phone, usually it's this kid named Tyler who sounds like he's half asleep, he goes, "Okay, so you need a MAP sensor?" No, Tyler! Mass airflow! MAF! I just said it! It's like the words go into their ears and just vanish into a black hole. And then when the delivery guy finally shows up, half the time it's the wrong part anyway. Last week they sent me a water pump for a completely different engine block. I had the customer's truck all torn apart on the lift, coolant drained, and I open the box and it's not even close to fitting. I had to leave the truck tying up my bay overnight while Tyler figured out how to read a parts diagram. But yeah, to answer your question again, yes, the voice and the tracking kept going for at least two weeks even when my mood was totally normal.

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve made mistakes at the shop and was pulled off high-voltage EV work because people were worried I wasn’t safe, and at home the fighting got bad enough that my husband took me for an emergency evaluation.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it definitely has. I mean, I’ve been making mistakes at the shop lately, which isn't like me at all. They actually pulled me off all the high-voltage EV work because they said they were worried I wasn’t being safe with it. 

Which, by the way, high voltage is no joke. You’re dealing with like 400 to 800 volts in some of these newer battery packs. You have to wear these thick Class 0 rubber gloves with leather protectors over them, and let me tell you, they get so incredibly sweaty in the summer. You’re trying to carefully disconnect a high-voltage interlock loop and your hands are just swimming in sweat inside the rubber. And if you drop a wrench across the wrong terminals... boom. Arc flash. It’s literally like a lightning bolt right in your face. I saw a guy at my old shop melt a 10-millimeter socket right to a battery post once. The whole bay smelled like ozone and burnt hair for a week. He didn’t even get fired for that, which is crazy when you think about it, but they pull *me* off just because I'm distracted by the cameras? Whatever. 

But yeah, it’s not just work. At home, the fighting with my husband about the tracking and everything just got worse and worse. It got so bad that he finally just packed me into the car and took me in for an emergency evaluation. 

He made me ride in his Prius to get there, too, which I absolutely hate riding in. The suspension is so mushy, it feels like you’re driving a marshmallow. I keep telling him I can put some stiffer struts on it, maybe upgrade the rear sway bar so it actually handles like a real vehicle, but he won’t let me touch it. He always says, "It’s a commuter car, not a race car." Like, I’m not trying to make it a race car, Mark, I’m just trying to make it so I don’t get seasick going around a basic cloverleaf on-ramp! It drives me crazy. But anyway... what was the question? Oh, yeah, daily life. Yeah, it's been a lot harder to keep up with things.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the patient’s mood episodes are severe enough to meet a manic episode threshold, which would favor schizoaffective/bipolar-related psychosis over schizophrenia or delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of at least one week when you felt so energized or irritable that you needed very little sleep?

target_item.name: Decreased_Sleep
target_item.manifestation: For weeks at a time I’d sleep maybe two or three hours, wake up before dawn with my mind already in the garage, and feel like sleeping more would just waste time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about periods of feeling energized/irritable specifically leading to a decreased need for sleep.

patient.answer:
Yeah, absolutely. There have been times, like for weeks at a stretch, where I'd sleep maybe two or three hours a night. I'd wake up way before dawn, and my mind would already be at the garage, thinking about all the work I could get done. It just felt like sleeping any more than that was a total waste of time when I had so much energy. 

Speaking of waking up early, the sunrise hitting the shop windows is actually really brutal if you're trying to read a scan tool. The glare is ridiculous. We have these big roll-up bay doors with those little rectangular windows in them, and the sun hits them at the exact wrong angle right around 6:30 in the morning. I told the boss we need to tint them or get some shades, but he just ignores me. He says it "lets the natural light in." Natural light, right. Tell that to my retinas when I'm trying to read live data off an OBD2 scanner on a car with a misfire. Have you ever tried to read fuel trim numbers on a tiny LCD screen while the sun is basically blasting a laser beam directly into your eyeball? It's impossible. You end up having to throw a jacket over your head and the scanner just to see the screen, and then you look like an idiot hiding under a coat in the driver's seat. And the scanners aren't cheap, either. The Snap-On one we have is like, five grand, and the screen is still awful in direct sunlight. But anyway, yeah, I'd only sleep a couple of hours and feel totally fine, just ready to go.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the psychotic symptoms occur only during mood episodes or also independently, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features and delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever heard the voice or believed you were being watched when you were not having any manic symptoms?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a quieter few weeks when I was sleeping more and wasn’t making huge plans, I still heard the garage voice and believed my husband and boss were tracking me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the psychotic symptoms (hearing voices, believing she is being watched) occurred in the absence of manic symptoms, which matches the criteria for psychotic symptoms occurring in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Doc, I feel like we're going in circles here. I know I just answered this. Yes, yes I did. Like I was saying before, even when I had that quieter stretch for a few weeks, where I was sleeping a normal amount and I wasn't running around making all those huge plans... I still heard the voice from the garage. And I still knew for a fact that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It's just like dealing with service writers, honestly. You tell them the exact diagnosis, you write it on the ticket—like, "customer states rattling noise over bumps, found worn sway bar links, needs replacement." You literally type it into the system. And then the service writer, who has never turned a wrench in his life, goes out to the waiting room and tells the customer they need new struts. No! I didn't say struts! Struts are like eight hundred bucks, sway bar links are fifty! And then the customer comes storming back into the bay yelling at me because they think I'm trying to rip them off. It's infuriating. The service writers just don't listen, they just hear "suspension" and try to upsell the most expensive thing. I swear, half my job is just fixing the communication breakdowns between the front desk and the customer. But yeah, to answer you again... yes, the voice and the tracking were still there even when I wasn't manic.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have occurred exclusively during mood episodes, which would favor bipolar I disorder with psychotic features over schizoaffective disorder or schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have there been any times when the voice or the belief that you were being watched happened for at least two weeks while you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a quieter few weeks when I was sleeping more and wasn’t making huge plans, I still heard the garage voice and believed my husband and boss were tracking me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the hallucinations (voices) and delusions (being watched) occurred for at least two weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (manic or depressed symptoms).

patient.answer:
Are you reading off a checklist or something? Because I really feel like we just went over this. But yes, to be specific, yes. There was a stretch of a few weeks where my mood was totally normal. I wasn't feeling down at all, I was sleeping a normal amount, and I wasn’t making any of those huge plans. But even during those quieter weeks, I still heard the garage voice, and I still knew for a fact my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

Which, honestly, is so ridiculously easy to do now. People think you have to be some kind of spy to track a car, or hardwire something into the fuse box, but you can literally buy a magnetic GPS unit online for thirty bucks and slap it on the inside of a frame rail in two seconds. Or those insurance dongles! Have you seen those? The insurance companies tell you to plug them into your OBD2 port under the dash to get a "safe driver discount," but it’s literally just a tracker. It logs your speed, your hard braking, your exact location... everything. 

We had a lady bring her car into the shop last month because her battery kept dying overnight. I hooked up my multimeter, doing a voltage drop test across all the fuses, and guess what? It was her stupid insurance tracker causing a parasitic draw. It was pulling like 300 milliamps while the car was off just so it could stay awake and beam her data back to corporate. I told her to yank it out and throw it in the trash. You can't trust anything you plug into a data port, they're basically just little snitches. 

But anyway... what did you ask? Oh, right, the two weeks. Yeah, for at least a couple weeks, I wasn't up or down, but the voice and the tracking stuff definitely didn't stop.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the psychotic symptoms are confined to mood episodes or occur independently, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features and delusional disorder
doctor.question: Have you ever had hallucinations or beliefs that people were watching you for at least two weeks when you were not having any mood episode at all?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a quieter few weeks when I was sleeping more and wasn’t making huge plans, I still heard the garage voice and believed my husband and boss were tracking me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is again asking if the hallucinations or delusions occurred for at least two weeks in the absence of a mood episode, which directly maps to Additional Requirement 3.

patient.answer:
Are you serious right now? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills. We literally just talked about this! I just said yes to this exact same question! 

But fine, yes, I'll say it again. Yes, there was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't manic, I wasn't depressed, I was sleeping fine, not making any wild plans... but I still heard the voice from the garage, and I still knew my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It’s like when a customer brings in a car for a check engine light, right? And you scan it, and it throws a P0420 code, which is catalyst system efficiency below threshold. So you tell the customer, "Hey, your catalytic converter is shot, it needs to be replaced." And they say, "Okay, but can you just clear the code and see if it comes back?" And you're like, "Buddy, I can clear the code, but the cat is still hollowed out, the code is going to come back the second the monitor runs." But they insist. So you clear it. They drive away. Two days later, they're back, complaining that the light is on again, asking the exact same question. "Why is the light on?" Because your catalytic converter is dead! I already told you this! It's like nobody listens to the actual diagnosis the first time. You can clear the code all you want, but the underlying problem doesn't just magically disappear because you hit a button on a scanner. 

Anyway. Yes. The voice and the tracking were still there for a few weeks even when my mood was totally normal. Can we please move on to a different question now?

doctor.intent: To distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder by checking for other psychotic symptoms, especially formal thought disorder/disorganized speech.
doctor.question: Besides hearing the voice and feeling watched, do you ever have trouble keeping your thoughts or speech organized, like others say you’re hard to follow?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized thoughts or speech (e.g., derailment, incoherence), which is not present in my symptom profile. (I have pressured speech, but that is about speed and volume, not disorganization).

patient.answer:
No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever told me I'm hard to follow. Sometimes I just have a lot to say, you know? Like, there's a lot going on in my head, especially when I'm trying to explain something complicated. 

But people usually get what I'm saying. Unless they're just not listening, which, like I said, happens all the time at the shop. Speaking of the shop, I actually need to get back there soon. We've got this nightmare of a job coming in this afternoon—a 2015 Ford F-150, the one with the 3.5 EcoBoost. The customer says it's got a rattle on cold start, which everyone knows is the cam phasers. It's always the cam phasers on those engines. Ford even put out a TSB on it, but the customer didn't want to pay for the repair when it was under warranty, and now they're out of the powertrain coverage and they're mad at us about the price. It's a huge job, you have to take the whole front cover off the engine, pull the valve covers... it's easily a twelve-hour job if you do it right. And the parts alone are a fortune because you have to replace the timing chain, the tensioners, the guides, everything while you're in there, otherwise they'll just be back in six months with a stretched chain. But try explaining that to a guy who just wants a cheap fix. He was in the waiting room yesterday just pacing around, looking at his phone... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my speech. No, I speak perfectly fine. My thoughts are organized. People just need to pay attention when I'm talking.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview and identify the main presenting complaint.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a clear schizophrenia-spectrum psychotic illness with persistent auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions lasting about 10 months, including at least several weeks of psychotic symptoms outside any mood episode. However, there are also prominent manic episodes (decreased need for sleep, increased energy, grandiosity/overactivity, irritability) that co-occur with psychosis, making schizoaffective disorder, manic type, the best fit rather than schizophrenia or delusional disorder.
